Products belong to child categories, so each product's top-level category is its child category's parent. A top-level category with no parent (a product placed directly in one) would map to itself, so I use COALESCE to cover that case.

{"sql": "SELECT COALESCE(pc.name, c.name) AS category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN categories pc ON pc.id = c.parent_id WHERE o.status IN ('completed','shipped') GROUP BY COALESCE(pc.name, c.name) ORDER BY units_sold DESC", "assumptions": "Units counted only for completed or shipped orders; products in a category with no parent are reported under that category itself."}
Electronics sold the most units at 1,592, followed by Fashion at 1,516, Home & Kitchen at 1,502, and Sports at 1,406 across completed and shipped orders.

{"sql": "WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)::date AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status IN ('completed','shipped') AND order_date >= '2025-12-01' AND order_date < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY 1), g AS (SELECT month, ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS growth_pct FROM m) SELECT month, growth_pct FROM g WHERE month >= '2026-01-01' ORDER BY month", "assumptions": "Revenue is total_amount of completed and shipped orders; December 2025 is used as the baseline for January 2026, and November 2026 is a partial month (data ends 2026-11-15)."}
